description: How traits are inherited, how allele frequencies change in populations, and how genomic data is used to map genes and predict traits. In the lab students simulate crosses and populations, test Hardy-Weinberg and structure, and run a small association study and polygenic score from scratch.
modelledOn: Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis
Hartl and Clark, Principles of Population Genetics
Lynch and Walsh, Genetics and Analysis of Quantitative Traits (selected chapters)
outcomes: Predict offspring ratios for Mendelian, sex-linked and quantitative traits and test them with chi-square statistics.
Estimate recombination fractions, map distances and LOD scores from crosses and pedigrees.
Test Hardy-Weinberg proportions and model the effects of drift, selection, mutation and migration on allele frequencies.
Describe and compute population structure with F-statistics, principal components and admixture models.
Run, quality-control and interpret a genome-wide association scan, including multiple-testing and stratification corrections.
Build and evaluate a polygenic score and explain its limits across ancestries.

units.title: Mendelian inheritance
topics: Mendel's laws, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, Punnett squares and chi-square goodness of fit
Dominance, codominance, incomplete dominance, epistasis, penetrance and expressivity
Sex-linked and mitochondrial inheritance; X inactivation
Genes, alleles and variants at the molecular level: SNPs, indels and copy-number variants
Worked cases from West Africa: sickle cell (HbS), G6PD deficiency and malaria protection
Probability rules in genetics: product, sum and binomial rules, and Bayes' rule for risk

units.title: Quantitative inheritance
topics: Polygenic traits, the normal distribution and the additive model of genotype effects
Variance components: genetic, environmental, additive, dominance and epistatic variance
Broad-sense and narrow-sense heritability; parent-offspring regression and twin studies
The breeder's equation and response to selection in crops and livestock such as cassava, cocoa and cattle
Genotype-by-environment interaction and reaction norms

units.title: Pedigrees and linkage analysis
topics: Pedigree notation and recognising autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive and X-linked patterns
Recombination, genetic distance, Haldane and Kosambi mapping functions
Three-point test crosses, gene order and interference
LOD scores and parametric linkage analysis
Carrier risk in pedigrees with Bayesian updating
Variation in recombination rate: hotspots and sex differences

units.title: Allele frequencies and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
topics: Allele and genotype frequencies; the Hardy-Weinberg principle and its assumptions
Testing equilibrium: chi-square and exact tests, and genotyping error as a cause of deviation
Inbreeding coefficient, identity by descent and consanguinity
Multiple alleles and X-linked loci; estimating frequencies by expectation-maximisation (ABO blood groups)
Non-random mating: assortative mating and its effect on genotype frequencies

units.title: Drift, selection and the coalescent
topics: Genetic drift in the Wright-Fisher model; fixation probability and effective population size
Natural selection: fitness, selection coefficient and heterozygote advantage (sickle cell as balanced polymorphism)
Mutation-selection balance, migration and gene flow; the island model
Neutral theory and the site frequency spectrum
Coalescent theory: genealogies, time to the most recent common ancestor and simulation
Detecting selection: Tajima's D, extended haplotype homozygosity and Fst outlier scans

units.title: Population structure and ancestry
topics: Wright's F-statistics, Fst and isolation by distance
Principal component analysis of genotype matrices
Model-based clustering and admixture proportions; choosing the number of clusters
Admixture and local ancestry; African genetic diversity, the Bantu expansion and the out-of-Africa gradient
Linkage disequilibrium: D, r-squared, haplotype blocks and LD decay
Limits and ethics of genetic ancestry testing

units.title: QTL mapping and genome-wide association
topics: QTL mapping in crosses: interval mapping, LOD thresholds and permutation tests
GWAS design and single-variant regression for quantitative and case-control traits
Quality control: call rate, minor allele frequency, Hardy-Weinberg filters and relatedness
Multiple testing: Bonferroni, genome-wide significance and false discovery rate; Manhattan and QQ plots
Confounding by stratification: genomic control, principal components and mixed models
Fine mapping, imputation and reference panels, including the under-representation of African ancestries

units.title: Heritability and polygenic scores
topics: SNP heritability and the missing heritability problem
Constructing polygenic scores: clumping, thresholding and effect-size shrinkage
Evaluating prediction: R-squared, AUC, calibration and portability across ancestries
Genetic correlation, pleiotropy and an introduction to Mendelian randomisation
Ethics and governance of genomic research in Africa: consent, data sharing and benefit sharing
Capstone: a reproducible pipeline from simulated cohort to association scan to polygenic score

schedule.title: Mendel, molecular variants and probability
schedule.exercise: Predict the offspring of a dihybrid cross, test the ratio with chi-square, and work out the chance that two HbAS parents have a child with sickle cell disease.

tasks.title: Simulate 1000 offspring of a monohybrid cross with Monte Carlo and test the 3:1 ratio against a chi-square goodness-of-fit statistic
Compute the chance that two HbAS carrier parents have a child with sickle cell disease, then across a family of four children using the binomial rule
Use Bayes' rule to compute the probability that a test-positive person carries a rare variant, given prevalence, sensitivity and specificity, and plot it against prevalence

schedule.title: Quantitative traits and heritability
schedule.exercise: Explain why height-like traits are bell-shaped, decompose a trait's variance into parts, and predict the response to selection from a heritability estimate.

tasks.title: Plot the distribution of a trait controlled by 1, 3 and 10 additive loci in 1000 simulated plants, and describe how its shape approaches normal
Estimate narrow-sense heritability of cassava yield from a table of parent and offspring values by regressing offspring on the mid-parent value
Simulate five generations of truncation selection on a trait of heritability 0.3 and compare the observed response with the breeder's equation prediction

schedule.title: Pedigrees, recombination and map distance
schedule.exercise: Classify five pedigrees by inheritance mode, convert recombinant counts into map distances, and deduce gene order from a three-point cross.

tasks.title: Classify five given pedigrees as autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive or X-linked in a counselling scenario, listing the evidence that rules out the other modes
Compute recombination fractions from backcross counts, convert to map distance with Haldane and Kosambi functions, and plot the difference up to 50 cM
Count recombinants from three-point cross data, deduce gene order and the interference coefficient, and check the answer with a simulation of double crossovers

schedule.title: LOD scores, carrier risk and recombination variation
schedule.exercise: Compute a LOD score for a small family, update a woman's carrier risk with Bayes' rule, and explain why recombination rates differ between sexes.

tasks.title: Compute LOD scores for a two-generation pedigree at recombination fractions from 0.0 to 0.5 in steps of 0.05, and plot the curve to find its maximum
Write code that updates a counselee's carrier risk from a pedigree using prior, conditional and joint probabilities, and check it against your hand calculation
Simulate crossover positions with a hotspot at 30 cM over 5000 meioses, then estimate the local recombination fraction and total map length

schedule.title: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and inbreeding
schedule.exercise: Compute allele frequencies for ABO blood groups from phenotype counts, test a SNP for Hardy-Weinberg proportions, and compute F from a village sample.

tasks.title: Count genotypes from 200 individuals at one SNP, compute allele frequencies and expected Hardy-Weinberg counts, and run the chi-square test with one degree of freedom
Estimate ABO allele frequencies from phenotype counts with an expectation-maximisation loop, and verify the estimates sum to one and fit Hardy-Weinberg
Implement an exact Hardy-Weinberg test for 20 SNPs with small counts, flag deviations after multiple-testing correction, and suggest genotyping error or a real cause

schedule.title: Genetic drift and natural selection
schedule.exercise: Predict from theory how long drift takes to fix an allele in populations of size 20 and 200, and find the equilibrium of a heterozygote-advantage locus.

tasks.title: Simulate 20 Wright-Fisher populations of size 50 starting at allele frequency 0.5 and plot the trajectories to see fixation and loss
Iterate the selection recursion for the HbS allele with fitness values you set, find the equilibrium frequency and compare it with the analytic formula
Simulate an island model with mutation, migration and drift, and find the migration rate at which populations stop diverging, comparing with the 4Nm = 1 rule

schedule.title: Neutral theory, coalescent and selection scans
schedule.exercise: Sketch a coalescent genealogy for six sampled genes, compute expected coalescence times, and explain how a selective sweep changes Tajima's D.

tasks.title: Simulate neutral allele frequencies in a large sample and compute the site frequency spectrum, comparing it with the expected 1/i shape
Simulate 1000 coalescent genealogies for 10 samples, estimate the mean time to the most recent common ancestor, and compare it with theory
Compute Tajima's D and Fst per window along a simulated chromosome with one sweep, and locate the sweep from the outlier windows

schedule.title: F-statistics, PCA and admixture
schedule.exercise: Compute Fst between three populations, interpret a PCA plot of genotypes, and explain how admixture proportions are estimated and how K is chosen.

tasks.title: Compute Fst between three simulated populations at 50 SNPs, rank loci by differentiation, and plot the distribution of values
Run PCA on a genotype matrix of 100 individuals from three groups, plot PC1 against PC2, and report the variance explained by each component
Implement a simple admixture model by expectation-maximisation, run it for K from 1 to 5, and choose K using cross-validation error

schedule.title: Linkage disequilibrium, admixture and ancestry ethics
schedule.exercise: Compute LD between SNP pairs, estimate the admixture proportion of a hybrid population, and explain what a commercial ancestry report can and cannot say.

tasks.title: Compute D and r-squared for SNP pairs from haplotype counts, and plot LD decay against distance to find where r-squared falls below 0.2
Estimate the admixture proportion of a hybrid population from allele frequencies in two source groups by least squares, with a bootstrap confidence interval
Respond to a community request to explain a commercial ancestry report in a scenario, covering what the inference can and cannot say and consent for reuse

schedule.title: QTL mapping and single-variant association
schedule.exercise: Locate a QTL in an F2 cross from marker data, run a single-SNP regression, and list the quality-control filters applied before an association scan.

tasks.title: Run single-marker regression of a trait on 5 markers in an F2 cross, plot LOD against position, and locate the QTL peak
Run per-SNP linear regression for 1000 SNPs and 500 individuals with one planted causal variant, and report the top hit's effect size, standard error and p-value
Apply call-rate, minor allele frequency and Hardy-Weinberg filters and a relatedness check to a messy genotype file, reporting how many variants and samples each step removes

schedule.title: Multiple testing, stratification and fine mapping
schedule.exercise: Read a Manhattan and QQ plot, explain genomic inflation, and decide which loci in a results table pass genome-wide significance.

tasks.title: Draw a Manhattan plot and QQ plot from a supplied results table, mark the 5e-8 line, and list loci passing Bonferroni and FDR thresholds
Show inflated test statistics in a GWAS with hidden population structure by computing lambda, then correct it by adding the first two principal components
Fine-map a locus with 30 SNPs in strong LD by computing posterior inclusion probabilities and a 95 percent credible set, then repeat with a smaller reference panel

schedule.title: SNP heritability and building polygenic scores
schedule.exercise: Compare heritability estimated from twins and from SNPs, build a polygenic score by clumping and thresholding, and explain why accuracy drops across ancestries.

tasks.title: Compute heritability from monozygotic and dizygotic twin correlations with Falconer's formula and compare it with a supplied SNP-based estimate
Build a polygenic score with clumping and p-value thresholding on a training cohort, and test its R-squared in a held-out set of 500 individuals
Compare score accuracy in a target set of different ancestry from the training set, quantify the drop in R-squared, and explain it through allele frequencies and LD

schedule.title: Pleiotropy, ethics and the capstone pipeline
schedule.exercise: Estimate a genetic correlation, critique a consent form for a community genomics study, and assemble a reproducible pipeline from simulated cohort to polygenic score.

tasks.title: Review a consent form for a community genomic study in a scenario, mark where it fails to explain data sharing, return of results and withdrawal, and suggest plain-language fixes
Estimate the genetic correlation between two simulated traits, and a Mendelian randomisation causal effect from three genetic instruments using the Wald ratio
Assemble a reproducible pipeline that simulates a cohort, runs quality control, an association scan and a polygenic score, and writes one report recording every seed
